title: Ringmaster
summary: Runs every local Laravel and PHP project from one place on Windows, each on its own PHP version.
body:
Ringmaster runs all your local Laravel and PHP projects from one place on Windows, using the PHP and Node already installed on the machine.

Local PHP work on Windows usually means one active PHP version at a time and a wall of terminals: artisan serve, Vite and a queue worker for every project. Ringmaster is a single daemon that supervises all of them, controlled from a web UI, a desktop app or the CLI.

highlights.title: A PHP version per project
highlights.text: Each project resolves to a real php.exe from the installs already on the machine. 8.2 and 8.4 run side by side and nothing global is switched.

highlights.title: Stopped means stopped
highlights.text: Every task runs inside a Windows Job Object, so stopping it takes the whole process tree with it and the port is freed.

highlights.title: Ports that never collide
highlights.text: The port is checked before a start. If something holds it, Ringmaster names the PID and the program. Projects without a fixed port get a unique one from a range.

highlights.title: Phone testing that survives DHCP
highlights.text: Binding to the LAN re-detects the machine's address on every start, so yesterday's config still works after the router restarts.

highlights.title: Careful cleanup after a crash
highlights.text: It cleans up the processes it started, and checks each PID's identity first so it never kills an unrelated program that reused the number.

coverAlt: Ringmaster web UI listing three projects, the tasks of one of them with their status, and a live log pane
coverCaption: The web UI running Ringmaster’s bundled demo registry. Captured on Linux, so the paths show /usr/bin/php rather than a Windows PHP install.
